title: A repo digest that beats reading the files, at the same context budget
problem:
Point an agent at an unfamiliar repository and it burns most of its budget finding out what is where. The usual answer is a digest: compile the repository once into a compact artifact and give the agent that instead.
Nobody publishes the comparison that matters. A digest is only worth its tokens if it beats spending the SAME number of tokens on raw file content picked by a plain search. Beat that baseline, on questions whose answers can be checked.

acceptance.how:
Your repo runs `make eval` against a public repository at a pinned commit and a question set, both named in the README. Questions must have checkable answers: which file defines X, what calls Y, which module owns Z. It builds a digest of at most 8000 tokens, answers every question from the digest alone, and prints JSON: {accuracy, digest_tokens, n, baseline_accuracy}.
baseline_accuracy is the same question set answered from 8000 tokens of raw file content selected by grep, and your repo has to run that arm too. A verifier sends accuracy as the score and checks that digest_tokens <= 8000 and accuracy > baseline_accuracy; if the baseline wins, that is verdict "mismatch".
acceptance.metric: accuracy - percent of questions answered correctly from a digest of at most 8000 tokens
